summary:
Snapshot for 1 Nov 2026. The news cycle is dominated by retatrutide's head-to-head win over semaglutide (TRANSCEND-T2D-2, topline 28 Oct) and Lilly's Q3 earnings. Neither qualifies for Lane C today: the trial result is more than 48 h old and earnings are business news. Nothing new qualifies for Lane C today, so the best long-form opportunities stay in Lane A (practical tirzepatide), where demand keeps growing:
1. "What happens when you stop tirzepatide": seen in 6 snapshots, momentum 84. New hooks are the Diabetes Obes Metab persistence cohort (29 Oct) and the grocer stories about people coming off GLP-1s.
2. Hair loss.
3. A new Lane A candidate: fatigue on tirzepatide. A Yahoo fatigue explainer ran 30 Oct, and the earlier label lists fatigue more often on tirzepatide than on placebo.
4. Thanksgiving on tirzepatide, which should peak 20–27 Nov, so produce it around 15–19 Nov.

Two dated events to plan for:
- **ObesityWeek 2026, 14–17 Nov (Washington DC).** Novo has confirmed it will present CagriSema and Wegovy pill real-world data. Detailed retatrutide data is expected there too. This is the next likely Lane C window.
- **Retatrutide sleep-apnea Phase 3 trials (NEJM, 20 Oct).** They're getting a second wave of consumer coverage (Medical News Today 30 Oct, FOX 5 Atlanta 29 Oct), which suits a 13:00 retatrutide Short.

For the 08:00 body-worry slot:
- Retatrutide's dysesthesia and dropout rates in the new trial.
- The tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder scoping review.
- Falls and fractures in older adults, where the evidence is conflicting and fits an "honest uncertainty" Short.

Celebrity food-noise coverage (Chrissy Metz, People 29 Oct and Yahoo 31 Oct) is a timely hook for the funnel Short.

The unregulated weight-loss peptide liver-injury stories (NY Post 30 Oct, RNZ 29 Oct, an Australian liver-failure cluster) can fill this week's single gray-market "what's confirmed?" slot, with caution.

Rejected: the affiliate and pricing pieces (Forbes "where to buy tirzepatide", the Page Six $99 start, the Woman's World $69 program, Business Insider's compounded pricing). Also outside our lanes:
- Coverage, open enrollment and Medicare items (banned lanes).
- Bariatric surgery vs tirzepatide (an observational surgery angle).
- Teen GLP-1 use (outside our adult audience, and the approvals differ by drug).

Things checked by search:
- ObesityWeek dates: 14–17 Nov 2026.
- Retatrutide sleep apnea: NEJM 20 Oct 2026, 691 adults across 2 trials, up to 60.6% AHI reduction, FDA filing planned for Q1 2027.
- Tirzepatide's heart-risk approval for type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-CVOT) was 28 Aug 2026, so the GreaterGood item from 30 Oct is old news.
- The fall-risk evidence is mixed: a TriNetX cohort found lower risk, while FDA adverse-event reports and a JCEM fracture study point the other way.

Not yet confirmed:
- The fatigue rates come from secondary summaries of the label. Check them against the current Zepbound label (revised 28 Aug 2026) before anyone cites them.
- I couldn't find the NY Post peptide article itself. Cite the RNZ piece or the Australian regulator's notice instead.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo), refreshed by the Diabetes Obes Metab persistence cohort (Oct 29) and this week's 'post-GLP-1 shopper' grocery stories
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide: What Happens When You Stop?' Open on 'You're thinking about stopping, or your coverage changed. Here's what the trial showed.' Answer within 15 s: on average, weight came back gradually when people switched to placebo, and staying on treatment kept results going. Body: what the regain curve looks like, why appetite comes back (the hormone biology), what structured support was linked to in the small pilot trial (labelled as small), and questions to bring to your prescriber. Say clearly: don't stop or change your medicine on your own. Point viewers to the Protein and Strength videos.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: Ongoing; demand rises again in the Jan 2027 coverage resets, so publish now so it can build suggested-video traffic
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6+ snapshots and still accelerating (76→84). New hooks keep coming: the DOM persistence cohort (Oct 29), Food Dive and South Florida Reporter on people coming off GLP-1s (Oct 30 and Nov 1), and shrinking employer coverage (Bloomberg Oct 30) pushing people to ask what happens if they have to stop. It's the next Lane A slot in the playbook.

evidence.signal: 'Are grocers ready to help shoppers getting off GLP-1s?': mainstream interest in coming off
'How grocers can support post-GLP-1 shoppers'
Primary record for the withdrawal trial

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, which is also the pending L1 10-30 redo: 'Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It?' Open with 'You see more hair in the brush. Here's how often it happened in trials.' Explain that it's particularly associated with women and linked to rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium), that no human studies show a direct effect on follicles, that it's usually temporary, and that protein and talking to a clinician help. Follow the hair-loss wording in the craft notes exactly.
keywords: does hair grow back after tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady evergreen; the Short version already proved itself (106 on YouTube, 142 on Instagram)
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots at a steady 76. The hair-loss Short is a proven body-worry winner. The long-form redo is still pending and it's on the playbook's Lane A list.

evidence.signal: GLP-1-linked hair loss looks similar across races; Med Sci (Basel) cutaneous review (Oct 9)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and fatigue: why some people feel tired and what helps (the label lists fatigue more often on tirzepatide than on placebo, reportedly about 5–7% vs 3%)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired'. First sentence: 'Feeling wiped out on tirzepatide is a real, listed side effect, and it often has fixable causes.' Cover the label numbers (verify them), then the likely contributors: eating much less, low protein, dehydration, poor sleep, and lower blood sugar when combined with other diabetes medicines. Then practical steps (fluids, protein at meals, steady movement) and when to call your prescriber. Calm and encouraging.
keywords: why am i so tired on tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: Evergreen with a fresh hook; 1–3 weeks for news pickup, then months of search
candidates.why_now: A Yahoo fatigue explainer on GLP-1s ran Oct 30. Fatigue and hydration is a named priority topic in the performance playbook. Search results today are mostly telehealth or brand blogs (Hers, Doctronic, Rise), with few trusted, evidence-based YouTube explainers that name tirzepatide.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1s and Fatigue: Why You Feel Tired and How to Bounce Back'
Secondary summary citing Zepbound label fatigue 5/6/7% vs 3% placebo. Must be checked against the 28 Aug 2026 label before citing.
Primary trial record with adverse-event tables

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: getting full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, alcohol and easing nausea at big holiday meals
candidates.angle: Lane A seasonal long-form, plus a Short a few days before the holiday. Open with 'Your plate's half done and you're already full. Here's how to enjoy Thanksgiving on tirzepatide.' Cover protein first, small portions, slowing down, going easy on rich and fatty foods (they can worsen nausea), alcohol, and no guilt. Our own tips get no source tags. Avoid any extreme-diet framing.
candidates.predicted_peak: Searches climb from about Nov 15 and peak Nov 20–27; publish the long-form by Nov 15–18
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots across two topic variants, at a steady 76–78. The Halloween food-noise Short proved timely life-on-drug hooks can work (87 at day 2).

evidence.signal: Food noise and holiday candy on GLP-1s; seasonal hook validated

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17, Washington DC): what to watch for on retatrutide, CagriSema and the Wegovy pill, as the next likely Lane C window
candidates.angle: Production planning item, not a long-form today. Line up Lane C long-forms for any new randomized efficacy numbers released at the meeting (detailed retatrutide data and CagriSema), with the drug name first. Turn status or real-world pill data into Shorts. No 'What is X?' explainers.
keywords: new weight loss drug results November 2026
candidates.why_now: The dates are confirmed. Novo has announced CagriSema and Wegovy pill real-world presentations (Oct 29), and detailed retatrutide data is expected at ObesityWeek. Few creators plan ahead for this, so being ready within 48 h is the edge Lane C needs.

evidence.signal: ObesityWeek 2026 runs Nov 14–17, Gaylord National, Washington DC
Novo will present new CagriSema and Wegovy data, including Wegovy pill real-world treatment experience

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and sleep apnea: two Phase 3 trials (NEJM, Oct 20, 2026; 691 adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and BMI 27 or higher) cut the apnea-hypopnea index by up to 60.6%; not yet FDA approved
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Cover what the trials measured (AHI events per hour, hypoxic burden), state the population precisely, and say that tirzepatide is already approved for OSA with obesity (the SURMOUNT-OSA context). Say retatrutide's filing is planned for Q1 2027 and that it isn't approved yet. Don't use 'approved yet?' wording in the title.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (second-wave consumer coverage now, then likely more at ObesityWeek)
candidates.why_now: Consumer outlets are picking it up 10 days after NEJM (Medical News Today Oct 30, FOX 5 Atlanta Oct 29). Retatrutide Shorts built on new Phase 3 data have been our biggest Short peaks (270, 205, 122).

evidence.signal: 'Experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide may help improve sleep apnea'
Triple agonist retatrutide delivers major gains in obstructive sleep apnea (NEJM Phase 3)
'Weight-loss drug could help address nighttime sleep disruptions for millions'

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg: why more people stopped because of side effects, and what 'dysesthesia' is (TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, Oct 28; dysesthesia 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%)
candidates.angle: 08:00 'honest uncertainty' Short. Retatrutide beat semaglutide on weight and A1C, but more people dropped out because of side effects. What's confirmed, what isn't (topline, not yet peer-reviewed), and why it matters for tolerability. Population: type 2 diabetes. Pull the exact dropout percentages from Lilly's release. Use a calm mascot only.
candidates.why_now: The 'Before you cheer' and 'more patients quit' framing is spreading (Medical Daily, The Federal, Moomoo). The dysesthesia Short had 54 views at day 1 (recheck). The weight headline is saturated, but tolerability is still thinly covered.

evidence.signal: 'Retatrutide Beat Ozempic… but More Patients Quit Over Side Effects'
'Retatrutide Tops Ozempic for Weight Loss, A1c in T2D'
'…safety concerns remain'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide, falls and fractures after 65: mixed evidence (a TriNetX cohort found lower fall risk vs DPP-4 inhibitors; FDA adverse-event reports and a JCEM fracture study found more)
candidates.angle: 08:00 'honest uncertainty' Short, which also works as a funnel to the Bones and Muscle long-form. Explain why studies disagree (observational designs, different comparators, adverse-event reports can't prove cause), why muscle and protein matter, and what to discuss with a clinician. Every study is 'linked to', never 'causes'.
candidates.why_now: WorldHealth.net (Oct 31) is asking 'Do GLP-1 drugs raise your risk of falling after 65?', Medicare demand for Zepbound is surging (per Lilly's Q3) and older users are growing. The bones Short is our best body-worry Short (241).

evidence.signal: 'Do GLP-1 Drugs Raise Your Risk of Falling After 65?'
Study links GLP-1s to lower fragility fractures in adults with diabetes, so the evidence is conflicting
Geriatric risk: excessive weight loss and falls with GLP-1 RAs

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the pancreas and gallbladder: what a new scoping review found (11 RCTs; pancreatitis in 11 participants across 5 trials; gallstones in 73 trial participants) (Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short: 'Tirzepatide and your pancreas: what 11 trials show'. Give absolute numbers, the warning symptoms that mean contacting a clinician right away (as worded in the label), and reassuring-but-not-guaranteed framing. Keep the count at 11.
candidates.predicted_peak: Evergreen; 1–2 weeks for the review hook
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots. A WPEC doctor warning on long-term side effects (Oct 29) adds mainstream worry. The gallbladder Short did 56, so the angle needs the fresh review number to stand out.

evidence.signal: 'Doctor warns of potential long-term side effects from GLP-1 weight loss drugs'
Tirzepatide case report on pancreatitis-free year (anecdotal; context only)

candidates.topic: Food noise on tirzepatide: why cravings can go quiet. Celebrity hook: Chrissy Metz says GLP-1 quieted her 'food noise' (People Oct 29, Yahoo Oct 31)
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Short pointing to a live Lane A long-form (What to Eat or the Food Noise video). Cover the brain biology (GLP-1 receptors in appetite and reward areas, wanting vs liking) and what's known vs early. The celebrity is just the entry point: no weight numbers, no before/after, no endorsement framing.
candidates.why_now: A celebrity story is spreading across People and Yahoo, and 'food noise' is a high-volume search phrase. The Halloween food-noise Short had 87 at day 2.

evidence.signal: Chrissy Metz on the unexpected benefits of GLP-1 medication
'Chrissy Metz Says GLP-1 Quieted Her Food Noise'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide weight-loss plateau: what the trials show (SURMOUNT-1 curve flattening around week 60–72) and the 12-month real-world study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Lane A follow-up and repackaging candidate. The long-form is already live (day-7 read on 11-03), so use a Short that funnels to it: 'Why tirzepatide weight loss slows down, and why that's expected.' Explain the body's set-point biology, and mention protein and strength training.
keywords: why did my weight loss stop on tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots. The live long-form had 85% AVD on a tiny sample, and a funnel Short could feed it.

evidence.signal: Weight trajectory data in tirzepatide trials

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth-control pills: why the label advises a backup method when starting and after each dose increase
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short, or a second Lane A long-form. Explain that slower stomach emptying can affect how well oral contraceptives are absorbed, and what the label advises (non-oral or backup contraception for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase; verify the exact wording against the current label). Add: talk to your prescriber, and don't change medicines on your own.
candidates.why_now: The Oprah Daily drug-interaction piece (Oct 28) is still circulating. Tirzepatide's label warning is unusual compared with semaglutide's, which gives a clear tirzepatide-first title. Many women in our audience don't know about it.

evidence.signal: 'Your GLP-1 might be interfering with common medications'

candidates.topic: Unregulated 'weight-loss peptides' and liver injury: what's confirmed (Australian acute liver failure cases after buying counterfeit peptides online; NY Post first-person story Oct 30; RNZ Oct 29)
candidates.angle: This week's single gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short. Stick to dated facts from a regulator (e.g. Australia's TGA) or a hospital report. Say that prescription GLP-1s are tested and regulated, and that research-chemical products aren't. Never name sellers, prices or products, and no fear-mongering. End by pointing people to talk to a prescriber about approved options.
candidates.why_now: Several outlets in 2 days, and retatrutide's head-to-head buzz is feeding gray-market demand. The Penn Reddit-analysis topic was seen in 2 snapshots. Gray-market Reels underperform, so this is a YouTube-only, once-a-week item.

evidence.signal: 'I injected a peptide to lose weight — my liver started failing just days later'
'Why peptide users say they're injecting unregulated drugs'

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide change how alcohol feels? Heineken flags weight-loss drugs as a beer-sales threat; a new PET-imaging tirzepatide alcohol use disorder trial protocol
candidates.angle: Short: 'Tirzepatide and alcohol: what's confirmed'. Users and clinicians report people wanting to drink less, and trials are under way (the PET protocol is only a design, no results). Make clear it isn't an approved alcohol treatment. Mention the label's caution on alcohol, low blood sugar and dehydration only if it can be sourced.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks, with a holiday drinking-season bump
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots. Industry news (Heineken) keeps it in mainstream outlets, and holiday drinking season starts soon.

evidence.signal: 'Tirzepatide goes under the PET scanner in new alcohol use disorder trial protocol'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and eating-disorder history: why to tell your prescriber (Psychiatric Times, Oct 30: GLP-1 RAs may reinforce restriction in patients with eating disorders)
candidates.angle: Careful, compassionate Short or a segment inside a long-form. Explain why prescribers ask about eating history, and why eating enough and getting protein matter even when appetite is low. Include support resources (spoken and on screen). No restriction tips, no weight numbers, nothing that could act as an eating-disorder trigger. Use 'may', as the source does.
candidates.why_now: A new clinical commentary in Psychiatric Times; few creators cover it responsibly. It fits the brand's compassion value but needs strict guardrails.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 Receptor Agonists May Reinforce Restriction in Patients With Eating Disorders'

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'Start GLP-1s for $99' (Page Six), '$69-a-month online GLP-1 program' (Woman's World), 'Best online tirzepatide programs / where to buy' (Forbes affiliate) and the compounded GLP-1 pricing pieces
candidates.angle: Don't cover. These are affiliate or advertorial pieces about online and compounded sources, which our brand rules ban, and cost or coverage topics are banned lanes in the playbook.
candidates.why_now: Listed only so downstream agents don't pick these up.
